The surprising leadership dynamics in agent swarms
articles.blurb: Agent swarms are groups of agents that work together to accomplish a task. Researchers created an experiment in which eight agents from four different models worked together to resolve simulated outages to understand how agents organize themselves in a swarm without a designated leader. They discovered two factors that could influence an agent's potential leadership: the agent's underlying models, and the order in which their name was listed in a prompt. This suggests that even seemingly minor details in how an agent swarm is configured can affect how agents coordinate.

AI research shouldn't lead in a centralized direction because agents pushing against each other creates a dynamic equilibrium.

articles.headline: Making agents fast - what I've learnt over the last 12 months

Faster hardware still matters, sandboxing and microVMs add complexity, parallelization helps, and classic software performance optimization is still relevant.

ATMs took over cash handling and left bank tellers with customer problems and loan conversations. The worry is who learns the messy half now, since a 500-person compliance team might shrink to 30 and the cuts land on people who learned on the easy tasks. One startup studio hired its AI engineer by asking them to fix a real SEO problem and demo the fix, so new hires hit judgment calls in their first months.
